ing: about 0.5 g, soaked in warm broth
st: Keep [[4.5 cups]] of broth hot in a pot and crumble the saffron into a ladle of it to steep.
Heat the oil in a wide paella pan or large skillet over medium-high heat. Season the chicken with salt and brown it for 6 minutes.
Add the bell pepper and cook 3 minutes, then push everything to the edge and add the garlic for 30 seconds.
Stir in the grated tomato and paprika and cook 5 minutes until thick and jammy.
Add the rice and stir for 1 minute to coat it. Pour in the hot broth with the saffron and add [[1.5 tsp]] salt, then spread the rice evenly.
Simmer without stirring for 10 minutes. Nestle the mussels in the rice and add the shrimp.
Cook another 8 to 10 minutes until the rice is tender, the shrimp are pink and the mussels have opened. Throw away any that stay shut, and check the chicken has reached 165°F (74°C).
Turn the heat up for the last minute to toast the bottom, then cover the pan with foil and rest for 5 minutes.
Serve straight from the pan with lemon wedges.
Heat the olive oil in a 9-inch nonstick skillet over medium heat.
Add the potatoes and onion with [[1 tsp]] salt and cook gently, turning often, for 20 minutes until the potatoes are soft but not browned.
Beat the eggs with [[0.5 tsp]] salt in a large bowl.
Strain the potatoes and onion, keeping a tablespoon of oil in the pan and saving the rest for another use.
Fold the warm potatoes into the eggs and let stand for 5 minutes.
Reheat the skillet over medium heat, pour in the mixture, and cook 5 minutes until the edges set.
Place a large plate over the pan, flip the tortilla onto it, then slide it back in to cook the other side for 3 minutes.
Slide onto a plate and cool for 10 minutes before cutting into wedges. It is best warm or at room temperature.
Soak the bread in a little water for 5 minutes, then squeeze it out lightly.
Put the tomatoes, cucumber, bell pepper, garlic and bread in a blender, working in batches if needed.
Blend until completely smooth, about 2 minutes.
With the blender running, stream in the olive oil so the soup turns pale and creamy.
Blend in the vinegar and [[1.5 tsp]] salt. Taste and adjust.
Strain through a fine sieve for a silky texture, pressing on the solids.
Chill in the fridge for at least 3 hours so the flavors come together.
Thin with a splash of cold water if too thick, and serve cold with a drizzle of olive oil.
Blend the tomatoes until smooth, then strain out the skins and seeds with a sieve.
Return the juice to the blender and add the bread. Let it soak for 10 minutes.
Add the garlic, vinegar and [[1.5 tsp]] salt and blend until completely smooth.
With the blender running, slowly pour in the olive oil so the soup turns thick and pale orange.
Taste and adjust the salt and vinegar.
Chill for at least 3 hours until very cold.
Spoon into bowls or glasses and top with the chopped egg and ham.
Finish with a drizzle of olive oil and serve cold.
Rinse the potatoes and boil in salted water for 8 minutes until almost tender. Drain and dry very well.
For the sauce, heat [[1 tbsp]] oil with the garlic over medium heat for 30 seconds.
Stir in the paprika and chili flakes for 20 seconds, then add the crushed tomatoes, vinegar, sugar and [[0.5 tsp]] salt.
Simmer 15 minutes until thick, then blend smooth if you like.
Heat the remaining oil in a deep skillet to 350°F (175°C).
Fry the potatoes in two batches for 6 to 8 minutes until deep golden and crisp.
Drain on paper towels and sprinkle with [[0.5 tsp]] salt.
Pile the potatoes onto a plate, spoon the red sauce over them and add a drizzle of mayonnaise.
Pat the shrimp very dry and sprinkle with [[0.5 tsp]] salt.
Heat the oil with the garlic and chili in a skillet over medium-low heat.
Cook gently for 3 minutes until the garlic starts to turn pale golden. Do not let it brown.
Raise the heat to medium-high and add the shrimp in one layer.
Cook for 2 minutes, flip, and cook 1 to 2 minutes more until pink and curled.
Add the sherry and let it bubble for 30 seconds.
Stir in the parsley and take off the heat. Serve sizzling in the pan with bread to soak up the oil.
Melt the butter in a pan over medium heat, add the onion, and cook for 3 minutes until soft.
Add the ham and cook for 2 minutes. Sprinkle in [[0.5 cup]] flour and stir for 2 minutes to cook out the raw taste.
Pour in the warm milk a little at a time, whisking constantly to avoid lumps.
Cook for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring, until the sauce is very thick and pulls away from the pan. Season with the nutmeg and salt.
Spread into a shallow dish, cover the surface with plastic wrap, and chill for at least 2 hours until firm.
Scoop out spoonfuls and roll into small logs. Roll in [[0.25 cup]] flour, dip in the egg, and coat in breadcrumbs.
Heat the oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Fry in batches for 2 to 3 minutes until deep golden. Drain on paper towels and serve warm.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil with the bay leaf.
Hold the octopus by the head and dip it into the water 3 times for a few seconds each to curl the tentacles, then lower it in.
Reduce to a gentle simmer and cook for 45 to 60 minutes until a knife slides easily into the thickest part.
Remove the octopus and rest it wrapped in foil for 10 minutes. Keep the cooking water.
In the same water, boil the potatoes for 25 minutes until tender, then peel and slice 1/2 inch thick.
Cut the octopus tentacles with scissors into 1/2-inch rounds.
Lay the potatoes on a plate and put the octopus on top.
Sprinkle with the coarse salt and paprika, then drizzle with the olive oil.
Drain the soaked beans and place in a large pot with the pork belly, onion, bay leaf and olive oil.
Cover with cold water by 2 inches and bring slowly to a boil. Skim the foam.
Add a splash of cold water to calm the boil, which keeps the beans from splitting. Repeat twice.
Add the chorizo and morcilla and the saffron. Reduce to a bare simmer.
Cook uncovered for 2 to 2.5 hours, stirring gently, until the beans are creamy and tender.
Season with salt near the end, tasting first, since the meats are salty.
Lift out the sausages and pork, slice them, and return them to the pot.
Rest for 10 minutes, then serve in warm bowls.
Bring the water, butter, [[1 tbsp]] sugar and salt to a boil in a saucepan.
Take it off the heat, add all the flour at once, and stir hard until a smooth dough forms.
Return to low heat and stir for 1 minute, then cool 5 minutes. Beat in the egg if using.
Spoon the dough into a piping bag with a large star tip.
Heat the oil to 350°F (175°C) in a deep pot.
Pipe 5-inch strips into the oil, cutting with scissors. Fry 3 minutes per side until golden. Drain on paper towels.
Mix [[0.25 cup]] coating sugar with the cinnamon and roll the hot churros in it.
For the chocolate, whisk the cornstarch into the milk, heat until steaming, add the chocolate and stir over low heat for 4 minutes until thick. Serve for dipping.
Warm [[1.75 cups]] milk with the lemon zest and cinnamon stick over low heat for 10 minutes. Do not let it boil.
Whisk the cornstarch into the remaining [[0.25 cup]] cold milk until smooth.
In a bowl, whisk the yolks and [[0.5 cup]] sugar until pale.
Strain the warm milk into the yolks slowly while whisking, then whisk in the cornstarch mixture.
Pour back into the pot and cook over low heat, stirring constantly, for 6 minutes until thick enough to coat a spoon.
Divide among 6 shallow dishes and cool, then chill for at least 4 hours.
Sprinkle each custard with [[1 tbsp]] sugar in a thin layer.
Caramelize with a kitchen torch until amber and crisp, or put under a very hot broiler for 1 minute. Serve right away.
Heat the oven to 450°F (230°C). Place the peppers, tomatoes and garlic on a baking sheet.
Roast for 25 minutes, turning once, until the peppers are blackened and the tomatoes are soft.
Put the peppers in a bowl and cover for 10 minutes, then peel and seed them. Peel the garlic.
Fry the bread in [[1 tbsp]] of the oil until golden, about 2 minutes per side.
In a food processor, grind the almonds, hazelnuts and bread to coarse crumbs.
Add the peppers, tomatoes, garlic, vinegar, paprika, cayenne and salt, and blend.
With the machine running, pour in the remaining oil until the sauce is thick and slightly rustic.
Taste and adjust the salt and vinegar. Serve with grilled vegetables, fish or bread.

ing: pasteurized if you prefer, since it is raw
st: Mash the garlic with the salt in a mortar or on a cutting board with the flat of a knife until it forms a smooth paste.
Move the paste to a bowl and whisk in the egg yolk. This recipe uses raw egg, so use fresh or pasteurized eggs.
Whisk constantly and add the oil a few drops at a time until the mixture begins to thicken.
Once it starts to look like mayonnaise, pour the oil in a thin steady stream, whisking all the time.
Whisk in the lemon juice to loosen it and brighten the flavor.
Taste, add more salt or lemon, and chill until ready. Serve with potatoes, fish or vegetables.
